questions.question: If you connect two identical bulbs to the same battery, how does their brightness in a parallel circuit compare to their brightness in a series circuit?
options: The bulbs in parallel are dimmer than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel are brighter than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel have the exact same brightness as the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel will not light up at all, unlike the series bulbs.

questions.question: How does the rate of energy transfer from a battery compare when lighting two bulbs in parallel versus lighting them in series?
options: Two bulbs in parallel transfer energy from the battery more quickly than two in series.
Two bulbs in series transfer energy from the battery more quickly than two in parallel.
Both parallel and series circuits transfer energy from the battery at the exact same rate.
No energy is transferred from the battery when the bulbs are connected in parallel.

questions.question: A battery is used to power two bulbs. How does the lifetime of the battery compare when the bulbs are connected in parallel versus in series?
options: The battery will run out at the same rate in both circuits.
The battery will last longer when the bulbs are in parallel.
The battery will run out faster when the bulbs are in parallel.
The battery in the parallel circuit will never run out.

questions.question: In physics, what does the term 'resistance' measure in an electrical circuit?
options: The rate at which energy is supplied by a battery every second.
How difficult it is for an electric current to flow through a material.
The total number of electrons present in the circuit.
The speed at which voltage travels along a conducting wire.

questions.question: How does changing the length of a conducting wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The length of the wire has no effect on its resistance.
Longer wires have resistance that fluctuates randomly.

questions.question: If you double the length of a uniform wire, what happens to its electrical resistance?
options: Its resistance is halved.
Its resistance is quadrupled.
Its resistance remains exactly the same.
Its resistance doubles.

questions.question: From a microscopic perspective, why does doubling the length of a wire double its electrical resistance?
options: It halves the number of electrons available to flow through the wire.
It doubles the number of 'atoms' (metal ions) in the way of the flow of electrons.
It increases the speed of the individual metal ions inside the wire.
It decreases the spacing between the metal ions so they are more tightly packed.

questions.question: What is the scientific definition of electrical 'power' for a device?
options: The total voltage pushed through a device over its entire lifetime.
The measure of the amount of energy used by or supplied to a device in one second.
The resistance encountered by electrons passing through a device in one minute.
The maximum current that can safely pass through a device without damaging it.

questions.question: Which of the following units is used to measure electrical power?
options: Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: When an electricity bill is calculated, what is 1 unit of energy equal to?
options: 1 watt per second (W/s)
1 kilowatt-hour (kWh)
1 amp-hour (Ah)
1 volt-ampere (VA)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit that has only a single continuous loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit with more than one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit where the current must flow through every single component in a single path.
A circuit that does not require a battery or any other power source to function.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the current through each individual branch relate to the total current through the battery?
options: The current through each branch is always equal to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The total current through the battery is divided by the number of branches squared.
The current through each branch is completely independent of the total current through the battery.

questions.question: How does the cross-sectional area of a wire influence its electrical resistance?
options: The greater the cross-sectional area, the smaller its resistance.
The greater the cross-sectional area, the greater its resistance.
The cross-sectional area has no influence on the wire's resistance.
The resistance is directly proportional to the cross-sectional area.

questions.question: Why does doubling the cross-sectional area of a wire halve its electrical resistance?
options: It doubles the speed at which each individual electron travels.
It doubles the number of electrons that can flow through the wire.
It halves the total number of metal ions inside the wire.
It prevents the metal ions from vibrating when heated.

questions.question: How does the voltage across each branch of a parallel circuit compare to the voltage across the cell or battery?
options: The voltage across each branch is half of the voltage across the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch is the same as the voltage across the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch is the battery voltage multiplied by the number of branches.
The voltage across each branch is always zero volts.
